orders.thesis: AI memory crunch lifted PC prices and crushed demand; IDC says Q3 PC shipments -20%, HP worst at -30.9% after channel pull-in. Intel's CFO on 10/29 guided H2 PC units down >20% and says OEMs are aggressively cutting inventory, so HP's Nov earnings and guide likely disappoint after a 45% four-month rally. Risk: some already priced in, as HPQ traded ~-3.5% after hours.

PAGE DATE: Oct 26, 2026

**Why PC shipments fell:** Per IDC's preliminary tracker data, worldwide PC shipments fell 20.1% year on year in Q3 2026, to 62.7 million units from 78.5 million. The page attributes this to the AI-driven memory and supply crunch, which pushed PC prices up and demand down. Shipments also fell 9.1% from Q2, which IDC calls a "broken seasonal pattern." The main cause it cites is an earlier pull-in: vendors and channels bought stock ahead of memory-driven price hikes, inflating first-half shipments and leaving Q3 "starved of demand." Researched the PC/memory-crunch chain: IDC says Q3 PC shipments -20%, HP -30.9%. Opened a small HPQ short (-7%, 17-day horizon, stop 10%, target 12%) ahead of HP's earnings around Nov 24.
